summary: The candidate covers nearly all headline results and most supporting constructions, including the handle formulas, gluing theorem, evaluation structures, and Khovanov test case. However, it omits the foundational functorial-link-theory definition, contains duplicated and partially conflicting gluing/Khovanov entries, drops some hypotheses or structural details, and has locator and notation inconsistencies. It is useful for downstream review but not fully reliable as a canonical mathematical entry set.
strengths: All four principal introduction-level results are represented: the 1-, 2-, and 3-handle formulas and the general gluing formula.

The candidate captures substantial supporting infrastructure, including the triple skein module, associated 3-manifold algebra, evaluation/module isomorphisms, gluing map, handle-specific subalgebras and submodules, and quotient formulas.
External background is often explicitly marked and attributed, including Morrison-Walker-Wedrich, Khovanov, and Ren-Willis.
issues: The gold definition of the functorial link homology theory and its two required axioms is missing as a candidate entry.

Several statements omit source conditions or structural details, such as the trivial algebraic-intersection/general-position condition for the triple and the cylinder local units for the 3-manifold algebra.
The gluing theorem is duplicated: one candidate entry gives an imprecise tensor product without the balancing algebra, while another gives the more accurate balanced tensor product.

The Khovanov test case is duplicated with inconsistent indexing, including a version using b in H^n instead of the boundary-state set B^n; similar duplication occurs for evaluation and handle results.

Page/locator metadata is incomplete or shifted for some entries, especially the headline theorems, and several raw entries lack normalized entryClass/title/sourcePath fields required for a canonical extraction.
